QF.id: VIII Introduction to Clearing and Settlement System_27

question.text: Final settlement of futures contracts on the expiry day is based on:

answer.text: The closing price of the underlying in the spot/cash market on the expiry day
The last traded price of the futures contract
The opening price of the underlying on expiry day
The average of the last 30 minutes of futures trading

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the source, the final settlement price for futures on expiry is based on the last 30-minute VWAP of the relevant underlying security or index across exchanges, i.e. the closing price of the underlying in the spot/cash market on expiry day. This is distinct from the daily MTM settlement, which uses the closing price of the relevant futures contract (computed as the last 30-minute VWAP of that futures contract). The Trap: Do not confuse daily futures-contract VWAP with the final underlying-security/index VWAP. The last-30-minute VWAP is used in both contexts, but the reference instrument differs - daily MTM references the futures contract, while final settlement references the underlying. Note: Source: NISM-Series-VIII workbook (Dec 2025), pages 34-35 and 155.
